corrections.why_refused: the release named 325 holds 325 clinical rows; the number of them recorded as GBM is a different, smaller count, read from the file
a C-index is a measurement, not a target: the recorded value comes from applying frozen TCGA coefficients to the CGGA rows
corrections.what_is_recorded_instead: see outputs_real\cgga_ood.json: the C-index per subset and file, recomputable from the cached zips; the pitch's 0.6412 is not carried as a result

corrections.why_refused: no four-state composition is predicted anywhere in this repository, and the GEO workbook maps cells to tumours, not to states
corrections.what_is_recorded_instead: single_cell_clone_fractions_from_bulk: PROVEN_FAILED in danon/genomics_intake.py; the dataset's reachability is recorded so the refusal is not a claim of unavailability

corrections.why_refused: the engine's EC50 is dimensionless, so an R^2 against a molar IC50 is a type error; and 34 of 34 temozolomide IC50s in GDSC2 are extrapolations beyond the highest concentration tested
there is no inverse-tensor estimator to score, and recovering an injected tensor is a self-consistency check rather than a measurement against tissue
corrections.what_is_recorded_instead: the forward operator is already verified against analytic solutions (check_solver_verified_against_analytic_solutions); no recovery figure is claimed

corrections.why_refused: a Dice forecast needs an expert mask and a second timepoint for the same patient; the live spatial_dice_verdict says no probed collection carries both
corrections.what_is_recorded_instead: BraTS-2021 segmentations are the committed geometry the engine runs on, not a forecast target

corrections.shown_in_the_pitch: sample code: `risk_scores = ages * 0.035` described as a TCGA-calibrated coefficient, `assert c_index >= 0.620`, and `from lifelines.utils import concordance_index`
corrections.why_refused: 0.035 is an invented coefficient (the repository fits age, sex and diagnosis on the real cohort and applies those betas); 0.620 is a threshold chosen before the measurement, which turns a result into a pass/fail rubber stamp; lifelines is not a dependency here, and the repository already carries its own Harrell C (danon/validation.py::concordance_index); and a test that downloads inside pytest makes the suite depend on the network
corrections.what_is_recorded_instead: the OOD test is a cohort script + cached file + claim check; whatever the transport C-index is, it is recorded as measured

notes: this validates a covariate model on external patients; it is not a validation of the treatment engine
no coefficient is refitted on CGGA: the fit is the TCGA cohort's and is applied unchanged, which is what makes this a transport test rather than a second internal validation
one external cohort at one metric is evidence of transport, not proof of 'zero overfitting': a model with no signal would read C~0.5, and a weak model can transport at the same 0.55-0.65 band
the model carries no treatment covariates; CGGA and TCGA differ in era and regimen, so this compares cohorts, not treatments
no imaging is linked to these rows, so nothing here is a spatial or engine validation
engine_caveat: this validates a covariate model on external patients; it is not a validation of the treatment engine
what_external_data_cannot_show: an external C-index over age, sex and diagnosis is a statement about those covariates, not about the spatial engine, which has no patient-level C-index at all
one cohort at one metric cannot demonstrate 'zero overfitting': it demonstrates transport, and a weak model transports too
CGGA clinical rows carry no imaging link here, so no growth or geometry validation rides on them
none of the five pipelines, even if all five ran, would make the engine's dose schedule validated: that needs outcome data tied to a treatment the engine chose
